sources.title: Speculations on Speculative Fiction: Is This Alastair Reynolds's Most Political Novel?
sources.author: Illusory Promise, 26 September 2018
sources.read_scope: Glitter Band abundance, diverse local settings and political disputes following the Aurora crisis.
sources.limitations: Later pre-plague setting context, not proof that every habitat has identical internal institutions or a second distinct economic regime.

decisions.reason: Automatic city maintenance survives, but the post-plague population's general access to necessities is not established in the short sources.
decisions.analysis: The account describes service/criminal livelihoods and inequality between Canopy and Mulch. Surviving automatic machines do not justify carrying over the earlier demarchy's guarantees.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading; do not manufacture a post-work or zero-variant point from the pre-plague system alone.

decisions.reason: A genuinely automated Conjoiner fleet factory is documented, but whole-population civilian access remains unclear.
decisions.analysis: Master of Works control of one secret project does not establish sovereign AI rule, general guarantees or a civilian nonworking fraction.
decisions.follow_up: Skip a deeper novel investigation in the faster pass.

decisions.reason: The Ultras are working interstellar crews and traders, not a verified common post-work welfare society.
decisions.analysis: Ship automation and long hibernation do not erase crew labor or establish labor-independent access for every Ultra.
decisions.follow_up: Preserve as a spacer-work comparison and skip deeper reading.

decisions.reason: The established pre-plague Glitter Band is already represented within the Yellowstone demarchy record.
decisions.analysis: The earlier record explicitly includes the participating habitats and their abundance/voting institutions. Orbital location and another novel do not create another materially different economic point.
decisions.follow_up: Link further same-regime evidence to the existing record. Split a specific habitat only if its production or access rules materially differ and are clearly documented.

decisions.reason: The broad Pattern-Juggler-associated lead lacks one identified community with clear automatic material provision.
decisions.analysis: A technology/ecology for storing or transmitting mental patterns does not itself establish a shared economic constitution. The quick check did not identify a qualifying allocation system.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading and require a named community plus a direct economic reference before reopening.

review_notes: Reference-led pass with explicit non-inclusions; no primary-text recovery undertaken.
Automatic military production, surviving city maintenance, hibernating crews and mental-pattern storage do not automatically establish civilian work-independent guarantees.
Glitter Band is an economic duplicate of the already encompassing pre-plague Yellowstone demarchy record; the duplicate is linked rather than counted again.
The Tampere thesis's direct open returned an Anubis access-denied page, which was respected. Its public indexed passage remains labeled indexed-only.
